lessons.title: Qu'est-ce qu'une galerie?
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand the purpose and function of art galleries

mindsOn.activity: Virtual gallery tour using photos or videos of famous galleries. Compare to other spaces students know: stores, libraries, theaters. Introduce vocabulary: GALERIE (showcase gesture), EXPOSITION (displaying motion), VISITEUR (walking/looking gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Photos of different types of galleries, comparison charts showing gallery vs other spaces, vocabulary cards with gallery images
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students have visited galleries: Build on their experiences and observations. If they haven't: Use familiar spaces like libraries or museums for comparison.

activities: Gallery Space Exploration (~9 min): Transform part of classroom into mock gallery. Arrange desks, create walls, establish viewing areas. Practice vocabulary: 'Voici notre galerie!' Walk through space as visitors.

Gallery Function Discussion (~9 min): Discuss why galleries exist: to show art, educate people, preserve culture. Compare to libraries (show books) and museums (show history). Practice exposition vocabulary.

Gallery Rules Development (~9 min): Create class rules for gallery behavior: quiet voices, careful looking, respectful movement. Practice 'visiteur' vocabulary while role-playing good gallery visitors.
materials: Simple artworks or posters for display
action.visualSupport: Gallery layout diagrams, behavior expectation cards, real gallery photos showing visitor behavior
action.decisionPoint: If students are excited about space transformation: Allow more time for gallery setup exploration. If they're focused on concept: emphasize gallery function and purpose.

consolidation.activity: Gallery Visitor Practice. Students take turns being visitors in their mock gallery. Practice appropriate behavior and vocabulary: 'Je visite la galerie.' 'Je regarde l'exposition.' Discuss what makes a good gallery experience.
consolidation.assessment: Can students explain what a gallery does? Do they use gallery vocabulary appropriately? Can they behave appropriately in gallery space?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students love the gallery role-play: Plan regular gallery visitor practice sessions. If they understand concepts quickly: Move toward more complex gallery operations.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Gallery exploration through pictures: Use art books or online gallery tours to explore gallery concepts, practice vocabulary through virtual visits.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Visiting museums, art shows, looking at displays in libraries or community centers

lessons.title: Rôles dans une galerie
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify different roles people play in gallery operations

mindsOn.activity: Role-play different gallery jobs using simple props. Show what each person does. Introduce vocabulary: CONSERVATEUR (organizing/selecting gesture), GUIDE (leading/explaining motion), ARTISTE (creating gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Photos of people in different gallery roles, simple costumes or props for role-play, job description cards with pictures
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are confused by professional roles: Use simpler job comparisons they know. If they understand quickly: Add more gallery roles like security or visitor services.

activities: Gallery Job Exploration (~10 min): Students try each gallery role. Practice curator decisions (what art to show), guide explanations (telling about art), artist creation (making art). Use vocabulary for each role.
Job Matching Activity (~8 min): Match gallery tasks to appropriate roles. 'Qui fait quoi?' Use pictures and vocabulary: 'Le conservateur sélectionne...' 'Le guide explique...' 'L'artiste crée...'
Classroom Gallery Roles (~9 min): Assign gallery roles for their classroom gallery. Students choose preferred roles based on interests and strengths. Practice role vocabulary in context.
materials: Role-play props (clipboard for curator, badge for guide, art supplies for artist)
action.visualSupport: Gallery job description posters, role demonstration photos, job responsibility charts
action.decisionPoint: If students all want same role: Discuss how galleries need all roles to function. If they're uncertain about roles: Allow job rotation and exploration.

consolidation.activity: Gallery Team Introduction. Students introduce themselves in their chosen gallery roles: 'Je suis conservateur/guide/artiste.' Explain what their job will be in classroom gallery. Practice professional vocabulary.
consolidation.assessment: Can students identify different gallery roles? Do they use role vocabulary appropriately? Can they explain what each gallery job involves?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students are excited about their roles: Begin role-specific training in next lessons. If they want to change roles: Allow flexibility and continued exploration.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Gallery job study: Use pictures and videos to study different gallery jobs, practice vocabulary without role-play activities.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding different jobs people do, like teachers, doctors, store workers

lessons.title: Sélection d'œuvres
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn to curate and select artworks for exhibition

mindsOn.activity: Present large collection of student artwork from previous units. Discuss how to choose which pieces to display. Introduce vocabulary: SÉLECTIONNER (choosing gesture), QUALITÉ (thumbs up quality), THÈME (grouping gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Large collection of student artwork, selection criteria posters, theme example cards
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If there's limited student artwork: Use art reproductions or simple classroom examples. If there's lots of artwork: Focus on selection criteria and decision-making.

activities: Quality Criteria Development (~9 min): Discuss what makes artwork good for exhibition: clear technique, interesting concept, good condition. Practice vocabulary: 'Cette œuvre a une bonne qualité parce que...'
Theme Exploration (~9 min): Group artworks by possible themes: colors, techniques, subjects, seasons. Practice 'thème' vocabulary: 'Ce thème inclut...' Compare different thematic organizations.

Curatorial Selection Process (~9 min): Students work as curators to select artworks for exhibition. Use criteria and themes developed. Practice 'sélectionner' vocabulary: 'Je sélectionne cette œuvre pour...'
action.visualSupport: Quality criteria visual examples, theme organization charts, curatorial process flowchart
action.decisionPoint: If selection is too difficult: Provide more structured criteria and guidance. If students excel at selection: Allow more complex curatorial decision-making.

consolidation.activity: Curatorial Presentations. Student curators present their selections and explain choices: 'J'ai sélectionné ces œuvres parce qu'elles montrent...' Discuss different curatorial approaches.
consolidation.assessment: Can students make thoughtful artwork selections? Do they use curatorial vocabulary appropriately? Can they explain their selection criteria?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If selections are very different: Celebrate diverse curatorial approaches. If students struggle with selection: Provide more guided practice with clear criteria.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Selection practice with art reproductions: Practice curatorial selection using famous artworks or art book images, focusing on vocabulary and selection criteria.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Choosing photos for albums, selecting clothes to wear, picking favorite books

lessons.title: Présentation et affichage
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn effective methods for displaying artwork

mindsOn.activity: Compare well-displayed art to poorly displayed art using examples. Discuss how presentation affects viewing experience. Introduce vocabulary: AFFICHER (hanging/displaying motion), CADRE (frame outline gesture), ÉCLAIRAGE (light gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Good vs poor display examples, frame samples, lighting demonstration
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students don't notice display differences: Point out specific elements like height, spacing, lighting. If they notice immediately: focus on vocabulary and technique refinement.

activities: Display Height and Spacing (~9 min): Practice hanging artwork at appropriate height for viewers. Learn proper spacing between pieces. Practice 'afficher' vocabulary: 'J'affiche à la bonne hauteur.'
Frame and Mat Exploration (~9 min): Try different frame styles and mat colors with same artwork. See how presentation changes perception. Practice 'cadre' vocabulary: 'Ce cadre améliore l'œuvre.'

Lighting Experimentation (~9 min): Test how different lighting affects artwork appearance. Use natural light, artificial light, spotlights. Practice 'éclairage' vocabulary: 'Cet éclairage montre bien les couleurs.'
action.visualSupport: Display technique demonstration cards, frame style comparison charts, lighting effect examples
action.decisionPoint: If display techniques are too complex: Focus on basic spacing and height concepts. If students master techniques quickly: introduce more sophisticated display concepts.

consolidation.activity: Display Quality Assessment. Students evaluate different artwork displays and suggest improvements. Practice vocabulary: 'Cet affichage pourrait être amélioré avec...' Focus on helpful, constructive suggestions.
consolidation.assessment: Can students display artwork effectively? Do they use display vocabulary appropriately? Can they evaluate and improve display quality?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If displays are very successful: Document techniques for future use. If students struggle with display: provide more guided practice with clear steps.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Display planning on paper: Plan artwork displays using drawings and layouts, practice vocabulary without physical hanging and arrangement.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Arranging their bedroom, setting table for dinner, organizing school supplies

lessons.title: Étiquettes et information
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create informative labels and descriptions for artworks

mindsOn.activity: Examine labels from various contexts: food labels, museum labels, store signs. Discuss what makes labels helpful vs confusing. Introduce vocabulary: ÉTIQUETTE (label pointing), DESCRIPTION (explaining gesture), INFORMATION (sharing knowledge motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of good and poor labels, label templates, information hierarchy charts
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle with reading labels: Use more picture-based examples. If they understand labels well: focus on writing effective descriptions.

activities: Label Information Selection (~9 min): Decide what information belongs on artwork labels: title, artist name, materials, date. Practice vocabulary: 'Cette étiquette inclut des informations sur...'
Description Writing (~10 min): Write simple descriptions of artworks using French vocabulary learned. Focus on clear, helpful information for visitors. Practice 'description' vocabulary.
Label Design and Creation (~8 min): Design labels that are easy to read and attractively presented. Consider size, font, placement. Practice vocabulary: 'Mon étiquette donne de l'information claire.'
action.visualSupport: Label information checklists, description writing templates, label design examples
action.decisionPoint: If writing is challenging: Use fill-in-the-blank templates or picture-supported descriptions. If students excel at writing: encourage creative and detailed descriptions.

consolidation.activity: Label Testing. Students read each other's labels and provide feedback: 'Cette étiquette m'aide à comprendre...' Test label clarity and helpfulness from visitor perspective.
consolidation.assessment: Can students create clear, informative labels? Do they use label vocabulary appropriately? Can their labels help others understand artwork?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If labels are very helpful: use them in gallery display. If labels need improvement: provide revision time and additional support.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Label analysis without creation: Study effective labels from museums or books, practice vocabulary through label evaluation and discussion.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Reading labels in stores, signs at zoo, instructions for games

lessons.title: Parcours de visite
lessons.oneGoal: Students will design logical pathways for gallery visitors

mindsOn.activity: Walk through classroom following different pathways. Notice how route affects experience. Introduce vocabulary: PARCOURS (pathway tracing), SÉQUENCE (ordering gesture), FLUX (flowing movement).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Pathway diagrams, visitor flow arrows, sequence planning charts
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle with pathway concepts: Use more concrete examples like following recipes or game rules. If they understand quickly: focus on sophisticated flow planning.

activities: Pathway Experimentation (~10 min): Try different routes through gallery space. Which feels natural? Which is confusing? Practice 'parcours' vocabulary: 'Ce parcours guide bien les visiteurs.'
Sequence Planning (~8 min): Decide order for viewing artworks. Should visitors see certain pieces first? Last? Practice 'séquence' vocabulary: 'Cette séquence raconte une histoire.'
Flow Optimization (~9 min): Design pathway that avoids crowding and confusion. Consider entry, exit, gathering spots. Practice 'flux' vocabulary: 'Le flux des visiteurs fonctionne bien.'
action.visualSupport: Gallery flow diagram examples, pathway planning templates, visitor movement pattern examples
action.decisionPoint: If pathway planning is complex: simplify to basic entry-to-exit flow. If students handle complexity well: include multiple pathway options and gathering areas.

consolidation.activity: Pathway Testing. Students follow designed pathways and evaluate visitor experience. Practice vocabulary: 'Ce parcours crée une bonne séquence parce que...' Make adjustments based on testing.
consolidation.assessment: Can students design logical visitor pathways? Do they use pathway vocabulary appropriately? Do their pathways enhance the gallery experience?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If pathways work well: mark them permanently for gallery opening. If pathways need work: continue testing and refinement.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Pathway planning on paper: Design gallery pathways using floor plan drawings, practice vocabulary through planning without physical testing.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Following paths in parks, routes through stores, order of activities in their day

lessons.title: Vernissage et inauguration
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan and execute a gallery opening event

mindsOn.activity: Learn about gallery opening traditions. Show photos of vernissages and art openings. Introduce vocabulary: VERNISSAGE (celebration gesture), INVITÉ (welcoming gesture), CÉLÉBRATION (party/joy motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Photos of gallery openings, invitation examples, celebration planning materials
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are unfamiliar with formal events: Use birthday party planning as comparison. If they understand events: focus on gallery-specific traditions.

activities: Event Planning (~10 min): Plan gallery opening: who to invite, what activities to include, how to welcome guests. Practice 'vernissage' vocabulary: 'Notre vernissage inclura...'
Invitation Creation (~8 min): Design invitations for gallery opening. Include important information: date, time, gallery theme. Practice 'invité' vocabulary: 'Nos invités recevront...'
Opening Event Preparation (~9 min): Prepare gallery space for opening: final artwork placement, pathway marking, welcoming area setup. Practice 'célébration' vocabulary while preparing.
action.visualSupport: Event planning checklists, invitation examples, gallery opening setup photos
action.decisionPoint: If planning is overwhelming: simplify to basic invitation and setup. If students love event planning: allow elaborate celebration preparation.

consolidation.activity: Opening Event Rehearsal. Practice welcoming guests, explaining gallery, conducting opening ceremony. Practice vocabulary: 'Bienvenue à notre vernissage!' Prepare for actual opening.
consolidation.assessment: Can students plan and prepare gallery opening event? Do they use event vocabulary appropriately? Are they ready to welcome guests professionally?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students are nervous about opening: provide more rehearsal time. If they're confident: focus on final details and hospitality preparation.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Opening event planning only: Plan gallery opening using templates and discussion, practice vocabulary without full preparation if time or resources are limited.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Birthday parties, school concerts, family gatherings

lessons.title: Visite guidée
lessons.oneGoal: Students will conduct guided tours of their gallery

mindsOn.activity: Experience difference between self-guided and guided gallery visits. Practice basic tour guide techniques. Introduce vocabulary: GUIDE (leading gesture), EXPLIQUER (explanation motion), PRÉSENTER (presentation gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Tour guide demonstration examples, explanation technique cards, presentation posture examples
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are shy about presenting: start with partner practice. If they're confident: focus on advanced tour guide techniques.

activities: Tour Script Development (~10 min): Write simple tour scripts for gallery sections. Include key information and interesting details. Practice 'expliquer' vocabulary: 'Je vais expliquer cette œuvre...'
Presentation Skills Practice (~8 min): Practice speaking clearly, making eye contact, using gestures. Learn to 'présenter' artwork effectively: voice projection, body language, audience engagement.
Full Tour Rehearsal (~9 min): Conduct complete gallery tours with classmates as visitors. Practice 'guide' vocabulary: 'Comme votre guide, je vous montre...' Receive feedback and adjust.
action.visualSupport: Tour guide technique posters, presentation skills checklist, effective tour examples
action.decisionPoint: If tours are too long: help students focus on most important information. If tours are too short: encourage more detailed explanations and interaction.

consolidation.activity: Tour Guide Evaluation. Students evaluate each other's tours using constructive feedback. Practice vocabulary: 'Ce guide explique bien parce que...' Plan improvements for real visitor tours.
consolidation.assessment: Can students conduct informative gallery tours? Do they use tour guide vocabulary appropriately? Can they engage visitors effectively during tours?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students excel at tours: prepare them for real visitor groups. If tours need work: provide additional practice and support.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Tour planning without execution: Plan gallery tours using scripts and route maps, practice vocabulary through planning without actual tour conduct.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Showing friends their room, explaining games to others, teaching family members new things

lessons.title: Critique et évaluation
lessons.oneGoal: Students will gather and respond to feedback about their gallery

mindsOn.activity: Discuss difference between helpful criticism and hurtful comments. Practice giving and receiving constructive feedback. Introduce vocabulary: CRITIQUE (analytical thinking), AMÉLIORATION (improvement gesture), FEEDBACK (response/sharing motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of constructive vs destructive feedback, improvement planning templates, feedback collection methods
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students struggle with criticism concepts: focus on positive feedback first. If they understand feedback well: introduce more sophisticated evaluation methods.

activities: Feedback Collection Methods (~9 min): Learn different ways to gather visitor feedback: comment books, surveys, informal conversations. Practice 'feedback' vocabulary: 'Les visiteurs donnent du feedback sur...'
Gallery Evaluation Session (~10 min): Invite other class members to visit gallery and provide structured feedback. Use evaluation forms. Practice receiving 'critique' constructively.

Improvement Planning (~8 min): Analyze feedback received and plan specific improvements. Practice 'amélioration' vocabulary: 'Nous pouvons améliorer notre galerie en...' Make realistic improvement plans.
materials: Comment books or digital feedback tools
action.visualSupport: Feedback analysis charts, improvement planning templates, evaluation criteria examples
action.decisionPoint: If feedback is overwhelmingly positive: encourage critical analysis for real improvement. If feedback is too critical: focus on constructive elements and manageable improvements.

consolidation.activity: Improvement Implementation. Begin implementing planned improvements based on feedback. Practice vocabulary: 'Grâce à la critique, nous améliorons...' Celebrate willingness to grow and improve.
consolidation.assessment: Can students gather and analyze feedback constructively? Do they use evaluation vocabulary appropriately? Can they plan realistic improvements based on criticism?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If improvements are major: plan extended implementation time. If improvements are minor: focus on continuous improvement mindset.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Feedback analysis simulation: Use hypothetical feedback to practice evaluation and improvement planning, focus on vocabulary without real visitor feedback.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Getting suggestions from friends, teacher feedback on work, family advice

lessons.title: Art français célèbre
lessons.oneGoal: Students will explore famous French artworks and artists

mindsOn.activity: Introduce famous French artists and artworks using reproductions. Compare to student artwork in their gallery. Introduce vocabulary: CÉLÈBRE (fame gesture), FRANÇAIS (France connection), PATRIMOINE (heritage/treasure gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Famous French artwork reproductions, artist biography cards, French cultural heritage examples
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are unfamiliar with French culture: focus on basic recognition and connection. If they have cultural knowledge: explore deeper connections and influences.

activities: Famous Artist Exploration (~10 min): Study 3-4 famous French artists and their most known works. Practice 'célèbre' vocabulary: 'Cet artiste français est célèbre pour...' Connect to student interests.

Cultural Heritage Discussion (~8 min): Discuss how art becomes part of cultural heritage. Connect to their own heritage and traditions. Practice 'patrimoine' vocabulary: 'L'art fait partie du patrimoine français.'

Artwork Comparison Activity (~9 min): Compare famous French art to student artwork. Find similarities in techniques, themes, or concepts. Practice 'français' vocabulary while making cultural connections.
action.visualSupport: French artist timeline, cultural heritage concept maps, art comparison charts
action.decisionPoint: If cultural connections are difficult: focus on visual similarities and basic recognition. If students engage deeply: explore cultural and historical contexts.

consolidation.activity: French Art Appreciation. Students choose favorite French artwork and explain why it appeals to them. Practice vocabulary: 'J'aime cet art français célèbre parce que...' Connect to their gallery.
consolidation.assessment: Can students identify famous French artworks and artists? Do they use French cultural vocabulary appropriately? Can they make connections between French art and their own work?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students love French art: plan deeper cultural exploration. If connections are challenging: focus on basic appreciation and vocabulary development.

lessons.emergencyBackup: French art study through books and digital resources: Explore French art using available resources, practice vocabulary through visual analysis without hands-on activities.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning about their country's history, famous people from their area

lessons.title: Techniques françaises traditionnelles
lessons.oneGoal: Students will try traditional French artistic techniques

mindsOn.activity: Explore traditional French art techniques: impressionist brushwork, pastels, simple printmaking. Connect to famous French artists studied. Introduce vocabulary: TRADITIONNEL (heritage gesture), TECHNIQUE (skill demonstration), HÉRITAGE (passing down motion).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Traditional French technique examples, technique demonstration materials, cultural tradition examples
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If techniques are too advanced: simplify to accessible versions maintaining cultural connection. If students have strong skills: introduce more authentic traditional methods.

activities: Impressionist Color Technique (~9 min): Try impressionist-style brushwork and color mixing inspired by French masters. Practice 'technique' vocabulary: 'Cette technique traditionnelle utilise...'

French Pastel Methods (~9 min): Explore pastel techniques used by French artists. Focus on blending and layering methods. Practice 'traditionnel' vocabulary: 'Les artistes français traditionnels utilisaient...'

Cultural Art Connection (~9 min): Create artwork using learned traditional techniques. Connect to French cultural heritage. Practice 'héritage' vocabulary: 'Je pratique l'héritage artistique français.'
action.visualSupport: Traditional technique demonstration cards, French art style examples, cultural heritage connection charts
action.decisionPoint: If techniques are challenging: focus on exploration and cultural appreciation over perfection. If students excel: encourage deeper technique development.

consolidation.activity: Traditional Technique Showcase. Students present artwork created using traditional French techniques. Practice vocabulary: 'J'ai utilisé cette technique traditionnelle pour créer...' Connect to cultural heritage.
consolidation.assessment: Can students attempt traditional French art techniques? Do they use traditional technique vocabulary appropriately? Can they connect techniques to French cultural heritage?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students love traditional techniques: plan more cultural art exploration. If techniques were challenging: focus on cultural appreciation and vocabulary development.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Traditional technique study: Study traditional French techniques through examples and demonstrations, practice vocabulary without hands-on technique practice.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning traditional recipes, games, or crafts from their own family

lessons.title: Galerie virtuelle
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create digital documentation of their gallery

mindsOn.activity: Explore virtual galleries online. Compare virtual to physical gallery experiences. Introduce vocabulary: VIRTUEL (digital gesture), NUMÉRIQUE (technology motion), DOCUMENTATION (recording/saving gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Virtual gallery examples, digital documentation tools, online vs physical comparison charts
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If technology access is limited: focus on planning and vocabulary development. If technology is available: create comprehensive digital documentation.

activities: Digital Photography (~10 min): Photograph all gallery artworks and displays professionally. Learn basic photography for documentation. Practice 'documentation' vocabulary: 'Je documente notre galerie avec des photos.'
Virtual Gallery Planning (~8 min): Plan how to organize digital gallery: categories, descriptions, navigation. Practice 'virtuel' vocabulary: 'Notre galerie virtuelle montrera...'
Digital Presentation Creation (~9 min): Create simple digital presentation or slideshow of gallery. Include photos, descriptions, audio if possible. Practice 'numérique' vocabulary while creating.
action.visualSupport: Digital photography technique cards, virtual gallery organization examples, presentation creation guides
action.decisionPoint: If technology is too complex: focus on planning and photo documentation. If students excel with technology: create sophisticated virtual gallery experiences.

consolidation.activity: Virtual Gallery Sharing. Present digital gallery to others. Discuss how virtual galleries can reach more people. Practice vocabulary: 'Notre documentation numérique permet de partager...'
consolidation.assessment: Can students create digital documentation of their gallery? Do they use digital vocabulary appropriately? Can they understand benefits of virtual gallery access?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If virtual gallery is successful: plan sharing with families or other classes. If technology was challenging: focus on digital literacy vocabulary development.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Virtual gallery planning without creation: Plan digital gallery organization and content, practice vocabulary through planning without actual digital creation.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Taking photos to share with family, video calls with distant relatives

lessons.title: Échange avec d'autres galeries
lessons.oneGoal: Students will connect with other classroom galleries or art spaces

mindsOn.activity: Discuss how museums and galleries collaborate and share exhibitions. Plan connections with other classrooms or local art spaces. Introduce vocabulary: ÉCHANGE (exchange/sharing gesture), PARTAGER (giving/sharing motion), COLLABORATION (working together gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Examples of gallery collaborations, exchange planning materials, collaboration possibility charts
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If other collaborating groups available: plan real exchanges. If no collaborators available: simulate exchange experiences and focus on vocabulary.

activities: Exchange Planning (~9 min): Plan what to share with other galleries: student artwork, techniques learned, gallery innovations. Practice 'échange' vocabulary: 'Nous pouvons échanger nos idées sur...'

Collaboration Preparation (~10 min): Prepare materials for sharing: artwork samples, technique demonstrations, gallery tours. Practice 'partager' vocabulary: 'Nous partageons notre expérience artistique.'
Exchange Activity (~8 min): Conduct exchange with other class/group if possible, or simulate exchange experience. Practice 'collaboration' vocabulary: 'Cette collaboration enrichit notre galerie.'
action.visualSupport: Exchange activity planning charts, collaboration benefit examples, sharing preparation checklists
action.decisionPoint: If real exchange is possible: facilitate meaningful artistic sharing. If simulated: focus on collaboration concepts and vocabulary development.

consolidation.activity: Exchange Reflection. Reflect on what was learned through exchange or collaboration. Practice vocabulary: 'Grâce à cet échange, nous avons appris...' Plan future collaborations.
consolidation.assessment: Can students plan and participate in gallery exchanges? Do they use exchange vocabulary appropriately? Can they learn from collaboration with other artistic groups?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If exchange was very successful: plan ongoing collaborations. If challenging: focus on collaboration skills development and vocabulary practice.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Collaboration planning and simulation: Plan gallery exchanges using hypothetical scenarios, practice vocabulary through planning without actual exchanges.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Pen pals, visiting other classrooms, community connections

lessons.title: Évolution de la galerie
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plan how their gallery will change and grow over time

mindsOn.activity: Discuss how galleries change over time: new exhibitions, growing collections, facility improvements. Plan gallery future. Introduce vocabulary: ÉVOLUTION (growth/change motion), CHANGEMENT (transformation gesture), CROISSANCE (expansion gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Gallery evolution examples, change planning templates, growth visualization charts
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students want gallery to continue: focus on realistic sustainability planning. If they're ready to move on: focus on learning transfer and future applications.

activities: Future Exhibition Planning (~10 min): Plan next exhibitions for classroom gallery: seasonal themes, new techniques, visiting artists. Practice 'évolution' vocabulary: 'Notre galerie va évoluer avec...'

Gallery Improvement Ideas (~8 min): Brainstorm improvements for gallery space and operations. Consider feedback from previous lessons. Practice 'changement' vocabulary: 'Nous changerons notre galerie en...'

Sustainability Planning (~9 min): Plan how gallery can continue without constant teacher support. Train student leaders, create systems. Practice 'croissance' vocabulary: 'La croissance de notre galerie nécessite...'
action.visualSupport: Gallery evolution timeline examples, improvement planning charts, sustainability strategy examples
action.decisionPoint: If sustainability planning is complex: focus on simple continuation strategies. If students are very engaged: develop comprehensive long-term gallery plans.

consolidation.activity: Gallery Future Presentation. Students present plans for gallery evolution and growth. Practice vocabulary: 'Pour l'évolution future, nous planifions...' Commit to realistic next steps.
consolidation.assessment: Can students plan realistic gallery evolution? Do they use development vocabulary appropriately? Can they take ownership of gallery's future development?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If plans are very ambitious: help students identify priority next steps. If plans are modest: encourage them to think bigger about possibilities.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Gallery future planning through discussion: Plan gallery evolution using discussion and planning sheets, practice vocabulary without implementation commitments.
lessons.realWorldConnection: How their room changes as they grow, family traditions that evolve

lessons.title: Célébration finale
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their gallery achievements and plan future artistic endeavors

mindsOn.activity: Reflect on gallery journey from first lesson to final exhibition. Celebrate growth and achievements. Introduce vocabulary: CÉLÉBRATION (celebration gesture), ACCOMPLISSEMENT (achievement motion), FUTUR (forward-looking gesture).
mindsOn.visualSupport: Gallery journey timeline, achievement documentation, future possibility examples
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students are very proud: allow extended celebration and sharing. If they're modest about achievements: help them recognize significant growth.

activities: Achievement Recognition (~9 min): Document specific achievements: skills learned, challenges overcome, growth demonstrated. Practice 'accomplissement' vocabulary: 'Notre accomplissement inclut...'
Gallery Legacy Planning (~9 min): Create documentation of gallery for future students. Include lessons learned, best practices, inspiration. Practice legacy vocabulary.
Celebration Event (~9 min): Conduct final celebration of gallery success. Include stakeholders: family, other classes, administration. Practice 'célébration' vocabulary during event.
action.visualSupport: Achievement tracking charts, legacy documentation examples, celebration planning materials
action.decisionPoint: If celebration is large: manage logistics while maintaining focus on student achievement. If celebration is small: ensure meaningful recognition of growth.

consolidation.activity: Future Artistic Commitment. Students commit to continuing artistic growth beyond gallery project. Practice 'futur' vocabulary: 'Dans le futur, je continuerai l'art en...' Connect to lifelong learning.
consolidation.assessment: Can students recognize and celebrate their gallery achievements? Do they use celebration vocabulary appropriately? Do they commit to continued artistic development?
consolidation.decisionPoint: If students want to continue gallery work: support transition to independent operation. If they're ready for new challenges: celebrate completion and support next artistic steps.

lessons.emergencyBackup: Celebration planning and reflection: Plan celebration activities and reflect on achievements through discussion, practice vocabulary without large celebration event.
lessons.realWorldConnection: Graduation ceremonies, end-of-season celebrations, family milestones

beginningSpeaker.description: Student uses 1-2 gallery vocabulary words with support, participates in gallery activities with guidance, shows understanding of basic gallery concepts
indicators: Participates in gallery setup and activities
Shows respect for artwork and gallery space

developingSpeaker.description: Student uses 3-5 gallery vocabulary words independently, takes active role in gallery operations, demonstrates understanding of gallery functions
indicators: Uses gallery vocabulary in appropriate contexts
Contributes to gallery planning and setup

expandingSpeaker.description: Student uses 6+ gallery vocabulary words in explanations, leads gallery activities, demonstrates sophisticated understanding of curation and presentation
indicators: Explains gallery operations using rich vocabulary

bridgingSpeaker.description: Student uses extensive gallery vocabulary naturally, demonstrates mastery of gallery operations, shows leadership and innovation in gallery development
indicators: Teaches and mentors others in gallery operations
Shows advanced understanding of art presentation and cultural heritage
